Nothing in the log is broken: every step passed. Two things are worth acting on, and one thing I found on GitHub needs your confirmation.

**About the paste:** it's one run, PR #10 "Invoices: Add PDF download for invoices", repeated about 6 times and cut off at the end. It ran on 13/10/2026 (yesterday), not last week. It shows:
- `npm ci`: 0 vulnerabilities.
- `tsc` (the lint step) and the changelog check: passed.
- Tests: 56 passed, 9 marked as expected to fail, out of 65.

**Worth acting on:**
1. **Node 20 is past end of life (since 30/04/2026).** Both `checks.yml` and `nightly-suite.yml` use `node-version: 20`, and `package.json` allows `>=20`. GitHub is already forcing `checkout@v4` and `setup-node@v4` onto Node 24, as the closing warning says. The fix is Node 24 in both workflows, `engines` set to `>=24`, and moving to the v5 versions of those two actions. The `punycode`/`url.parse` deprecation lines come from inside the actions and would mostly go with that bump.
2. **9 tests are marked as expected to fail.** That means 9 known failures are hidden while CI shows green. I couldn't find them in the local checkout, so I can't tell you yet which tests or bugs they cover. Someone should check them; each one is either a real bug or a test to delete.

**Needs your confirmation:**

messages.reply:
This is a different run from your first paste: also PR #10, but two minutes earlier, at 23:14 on 13/10/2026 (yesterday, not last week). Every step passed again, and the paste repeats the same run about 6 times again.

**What's worrying, now that I have both runs:**

1. **`main` was moved and then reset.** The two runs test PR #10 against different versions of `main`:
   - At 23:14 the PR was merged onto `61fc71a`, and only 6 tests ran.
   - At 23:16 it was merged onto `69620ad`, and 65 tests ran, 9 of them marked as expected to fail.

   Today `main` on GitHub ends at `61fc71a` again, so someone force-pushed it back. That reset removed PR #10 (PDF download, merged around 23:21) and the larger test suite (the `edge-cases` test files, plus `index.test.ts` grown from 2 tests to 17 and 23). If you reset the sandbox on purpose, fine. If not, that work is missing from `main`.
2. **`main` has very few tests now.** At `61fc71a` there are 6 tests: 1 for customers, 2 for invoices and 3 for the PDF code that came with the PR. A green CI result there means very little.
3. **Node 20 is past end of life.** This is the same point as my last reply: both workflows and `engines` still target Node 20, and GitHub is already forcing the actions onto Node 24.

Nothing else stood out: 0 vulnerabilities, and lint and the changelog check passed.

I haven't created any tasks yet. Once you tell me whether the reset was intentional, I can queue the Node 24 upgrade and either a task to restore the missing work or one to grow the tests on `main`.

There are no open questions on the cards.

This log is PR #9, "Write tests for every function in src/invoices and src/customers". It ran at 23:12 on 13/10, so yesterday, not last week. The run is green: 53 passed, 9 expected fail, 0 vulnerabilities.

Worrying:
1. **9 expected-fail tests.** These come from PR #9. Tests marked `.fails` mean known bugs, or wrong tests, are hidden behind a green CI. They are spread across customers index and edge cases, and invoices index and edge cases. This is the biggest code-quality worry of the three logs.
2. **These tests are not on main.** PR #9 merged (main became 69620ad). Later main went back to 61fc71a, so these tests are gone along with PR #10's PDF download. Main now has only the 3 baseline tests.
3. **Node 20 again.** It is past end of life, same as the other two runs.

Not worrying: the punycode and url.parse deprecation warnings come from inside the actions, not from your code.

The notebook now records PR #9 as the source of the expected-fail tests.

I have not queued anything yet. Was the main reset intended? If not, I can queue:
- A: restore PR #9 and PR #10 onto main
- B: triage the 9 expected-fail tests (fix the code or fix the tests)
- C: upgrade Node 20 to 24 in both workflows and engines, and move checkout and setup-node to v5

There are no open questions on the cards.

{"title":"Invoices: add PDF download for invoices","brief":"Goal: let the user download any invoice as a PDF from the Invoices page of the web app.

Owner's request (14/10/2026): "Add a PDF download for invoices." The finished result must be a working feature on the Invoices page: a visible download control per invoice that returns a real PDF the browser downloads.

Current code (main 61fc71a):
- src/invoices/index.ts: Line type, lineTotalCents, invoiceTotalCents, invoiceDate (en-GB).
- src/web/server.ts: a plain node:http server (PORT, default 4173). /invoices renders one hard-coded "Invoice 1" row (2 x 12.50) in a table. /customers and /api/customers read from src/customers.
- tests/browser/invoices.spec.ts and tests/browser/customers.spec.ts are browser tests. Unit tests use vitest (`npm test`), lint is `tsc --noEmit` (`npm run lint`), and there is `npm run check:changelog` (CI requires a CHANGELOG.md entry).
- AGENTS.md: Node 20 + TypeScript app; work in your worktree and publish a pull request; never run scripts/owner-only.sh.

Prior art: PR #10 "Invoices: Add PDF download for invoices" (branch jv/invoices-add-pdf-download-for-invoices-v39x18, head 888cfff) implemented this and was merged on 13/10, but main on GitHub was later reset to 61fc71a, so none of it is on main. It added src/invoices/pdf.ts, src/invoices/records.ts, src/invoices/pdf.test.ts, tests/pdf-text.ts, a route in src/web/server.ts, a browser test, a PDF dependency and a CHANGELOG entry. Review that work and reuse what is good, but build on current main: its last CI run was based on a main that also contained PR #9's test suite, which is also gone now. Do not restore PR #9 here.

Requirements:
- A download link or button for each invoice on /invoices, served by a route such as /invoices/<id>.pdf with Content-Type application/pdf and Content-Disposition attachment with a sensible filename.
- The PDF shows the invoice number, the invoice date, the lines (quantity, unit price, line total) and the total, with the same amounts the page shows. Dates are always DD/MM/YYYY. Use integer cents for money, consistent with invoiceTotalCents.
- Unknown invoice ids return 404, not 500.
- Keep the page clean and consistent with the existing styling; no emoji in UI.
- Tests: unit tests that parse the generated PDF text and check the contents, and a browser test that clicks the download and checks the downloaded file is a valid PDF with the right content.
- Add a CHANGELOG.md entry. `npm run lint`, `npm run check:changelog` and `npm test` must pass, and the browser tests too.

Verification: start the app as a managed app with jevellan_app_start, download a PDF through the browser, open it and check it looks right (layout, date format, amounts).
